title: Circuit-Breaker Escape Hatch Modal: keyboard-first rollback flow + telemetry snapshot
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and prototype a compact, keyboard-first 'Escape Hatch' modal for emergency rollbacks and circuit-breaker invocations in Redwood Console rollouts. This interaction is intended for on-call engineers and product owners who need to initiate rapid mitigation while seeing the minimal critical telemetry and rollback consequences. The modal must be fast to summon, clear about the effects, and reversible where possible (soft-revert vs hard-revert).

Goals:
- Surface only essential controls and telemetry for emergency decisions (error rate, latency spike, user-affecting percentage).
- Enable keyboard-driven invocation and confirmation (hotkey to open, Enter/Escape to confirm/cancel).
- Provide three rollback modes: Soft (traffic taper to previous stable variant), Quarantine (divert traffic to safe variant), and Full Revert (rollback to previous release).
- Show immediate cost delta estimate and expected latency change for each rollback mode.
- Include a one-click 'Snapshot & Reproduce' that captures request traces, recent sample responses, and links to the APM dashboard and incident timeline.
- Ensure WCAG AA contrast and screen-reader announcements for modal open, chosen option, and outcome.

User flows covered:
1) Keyboard hotkey (Ctrl+K then R) opens Escape Hatch modal from any rollouts or experiment view.
2) Rapid decision: choose Soft/Quarantine/Full by pressing 1/2/3; confirm with Enter.
3) Modal calls out automated fallback policies and shows which safety gates (SLO checks) will run post-action.
4) On confirmation, modal displays the immediate job progress with live token-level latency and rate charts condensed to mini-sparklines.
5) If user cancels, the modal records an audit event with reason.

Acceptance criteria (design):
- High-fidelity prototype demonstrates keyboard-only path from invocation to confirmation and shows failure states (failed revert, partial success).
- Visual treatment is compact (max 680px width), with clear hierarchy: title, critical telemetry, choices, cost/latency delta, action buttons.
- Prototype includes accessible labels, focus trap, and ARIA live region for progress updates.
- Content microcopy reviewed with Security & Compliance for audit trail wording.
- Handoff tokens defined: color tokens, spacing, motion durations.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype (keyboard-first frames + interactive flow). Link: https://www.figma.com/file/RedwoodEscapeHatchPrototype (placeholder link).
- Clickable InVision/Proto link for usability sessions.
- Design spec doc in Confluence: /docs/console/escape-hatch-modal (placeholder).
- Acceptance test checklist for QE and Eng integration.

Dependencies:
- Eng: rollout-api support for 3 rollback modes and rollback-preview endpoint (dependency: ENG-42100).
- Eng: lightweight telemetry endpoint returning aggregated 60s window metrics (dependency: ENG-41877).
- Security: audit-log schema confirmation (dependency: SEC-2045).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we allow soft-revert autoschedule (taper over N minutes) configurable in the modal? Trade-off: adds latency to the path but reduces user error. Decision: prototype with default taper of 5 minutes and an advanced link to edit schedule.
- Cost delta estimation accuracy vs speed. Decision: show an optimistic estimate range (+/- 10%) with link to full cost simulator in Rollout Details.

Next steps:
- Iterate prototype based on initial usability session (3 SREs, 2 PMs) by 2026-03-05.
- Ship design tokens and markups to Eng with specs for keyboard interactions and ARIA mapping by 2026-03-12.

Notes on uniqueness and constraints:
This ticket focuses on an emergency-first surface, different from the larger rollout composer/playbook prototypes. It intentionally compresses the decision space and couples the action with a minimal telemetry snapshot to reduce cognitive load during incidents.
